summary.en-US: Manage a Foundry VTT server's game systems, modules and Foundry updates from its setup screen: see what every world uses, plan updates that keep every world working, and install them through Foundry's own installer.

description.en-US:
EMMA, the Enhanced Module Manager Application, brings package management to Foundry VTT's setup screen, where you can
see every world on your server at once, before launching any of them.

WHAT IT DOES

• Shows your installation as a tree: your worlds, game systems and modules, and what each world last ran with.
• Finds updates for Foundry VTT, its game systems and its modules, and offers only versions that keep every world that
  uses them working, as Foundry installs one version of a package for all of them.
• Builds an update plan of installs, updates and uninstalls, explains why it takes each version, and runs it through
  Foundry's own installer, offering first to back up the worlds it affects and to take a snapshot.
• Installs new game systems and modules from Foundry's package listing or a manifest URL, with what they require and,
  if you want, what they recommend.
• Keeps Foundry's own package buttons from changing what EMMA is managing, until you switch it off.

WHAT YOU NEED

• A Foundry VTT server, version 14 or later, and its administrator password.
• A Mondarth account and an EMMA subscription, through Patreon or bought from Mondarth's accounts, to find updates and
  packages to install in EMMA's package catalogue. The installation tree works without one.
• The EMMA module, free on Foundry's package listing, active in the worlds you want EMMA to know in detail.

PRIVACY

EMMA runs only on the servers you activate it on, and asks for each. To find updates, it sends EMMA's package catalogue
the IDs, versions and manifest URLs of the installed game systems and modules, and your sign-in. It sends nothing about
your worlds, your server or you otherwise. See https://accounts.mondarth.com/privacy.

EMMA is not made by, nor endorsed by, Foundry Gaming. Documentation: https://mondarth.github.io/EMMA/ · Discord:
https://discord.gg/uJqFdjNsU4 · Source: https://github.com/Mondarth/EMMA

version.approval_notes:
EMMA runs only on the setup screen (`/setup`) of a Foundry VTT server (self-hosted, at any address), and only once
the user activates it there from the toolbar button, which asks for that server's host permission. It runs only the
extension's own scripts: one in the isolated world (the bridge to the extension), and one in the page's own world,
as it drives Foundry's own setup-screen client (`game`, `foundry`) to read what is installed and to install
packages through Foundry's own installer.

It talks to two services of its own: EMMA's package catalogue (https://catalogue.mondarth.com), which it asks for
updates, Foundry's package listing and manifests, and Mondarth's accounts (https://accounts.mondarth.com), where the
user signs in with a device code, from the options page. The catalogue needs a subscription; without one, EMMA shows
the installation but finds no updates.

To try it, it needs a Foundry VTT server (version 14 or later) and its administrator password. Either:

- on request, we set up a server for the review, and an account with a subscription, for as long as the review
  needs them; or
- run the whole thing yourself: get the source from https://github.com/Mondarth/EMMA, follow the developer setup
  (https://mondarth.github.io/EMMA/developers/setup.html), which runs a Foundry VTT server in Docker, with a trial
  Foundry VTT licence from Foundry Gaming, and load the extension you built (below) to use EMMA on its setup
  screen.

The build is bundled and minified by Vite from TypeScript and Svelte; the source is attached, and public at
https://github.com/Mondarth/EMMA. Building it is described below.

Requirements: Node.js 24, pnpm 12 (the version in the root `package.json`'s `packageManager`; `corepack enable`
gives it), `zip`, on Linux or macOS.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
EMMA_DEFAULT_CATALOGUE_URL=https://catalogue.mondarth.com/ \
EMMA_ACCOUNTS_URL=https://accounts.mondarth.com \
  pnpm --filter '@mondarth/emma-extension...' run build
```

The Firefox build is then in `packages/extension/dist/firefox`, as submitted. The two variables give the services'
addresses, built in as plain text; nothing secret is built in. `packages/extension/scripts/release/package.ts` is the
release's own script, which also zips and signs.

The source archive is `git archive` of the release's tag, `extension-v<version>`.
